title: Does an AI proposal writer really save me time and win more gigs? My 2-week test
excerpt: I spent two weeks using an AI-powered proposal generator on every pitch I sent. Here’s what actually happened to my workflow, response rate, and earnings.
metaDescription: I tried an AI proposal writer for two weeks. Find out if it truly cuts writing time, improves win rates, and is worth a freelancer’s budget.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Professionals reviewing documents at a meeting table
body:
## My hypothesis
I keep hearing that AI can draft a client proposal in minutes. The promise sounds great, but I wondered if the time saved is real or just a gimmick. More importantly, does a faster draft translate into more wins, or does it just produce more noise?

## The tool I tried
I signed up for **ProposalAI**, a SaaS that claims to turn a brief outline into a full-blown proposal with pricing tables, timelines, and a custom cover letter. The pricing is $25 per month for unlimited drafts - a modest cost for a freelancer testing a new workflow.

## How I set it up
- **Create a template** - I uploaded my standard service description, branding assets, and a few past proposals.
- **Define variables** - client name, project scope, hourly rate, and deadline.
- **Feed the brief** - a short bullet list of what the client wants.
- **Let the AI generate** - within 30-45 seconds I got a polished PDF.

I used the same process for every pitch I sent between Oct 15 and Oct 29. I kept a simple spreadsheet to track:
- Time spent writing (manual vs AI)
- Number of proposals sent
- Replies received
- Wins and earnings

## Results after two weeks
### Time savings
When I wrote a proposal from scratch, I usually spent about an hour polishing language, formatting tables, and adding a cover page. With ProposalAI the total time per pitch dropped to roughly 12-15 minutes - a dramatic reduction. The biggest gain was in formatting; the AI handled tables and styling automatically.

### Response rate
I sent 28 proposals in the test period and got replies to about a third of them. In the month before the test, the reply rate was similar, so I can’t claim a clear boost.

### Win rate and earnings
From the replies I closed three projects, one of which was a $1,200 website audit. In the previous month I closed two projects, the largest being $1,500. The sample is tiny, but I was able to send a few more pitches because each one cost less time.

### Quality concerns
The AI sometimes inserted generic buzzwords that didn’t match the client’s tone. I had to edit those sections, which added a few minutes back into the workflow. Also, the pricing table assumed a flat hourly rate; for tiered pricing I still needed to adjust manually.

## What I learned
- **Time is the real win.** Even if the win rate stays flat, shaving 30-45 minutes per pitch adds up over a month.
- **Human touch still matters.** A quick skim and a personal tweak keep the proposal from feeling robotic.
- **Cost-benefit balance.** At $25/month, the tool paid for itself after the first two closed deals in my test.
- **Scope matters.** For simple, repeatable services (e.g., website audits) the AI shines. For complex, custom solutions you’ll spend more editing.
- **Mental relief matters.** In my view, the biggest advantage is the mental relief of not staring at a blank document.

## FAQ
**Q: Do I need a deep learning background to use an AI proposal writer?**
A: No. The interface is built for non-technical freelancers. You only need to supply a brief and a template.

**Q: Will clients notice the AI-generated language?**
A: Most won’t. If you keep the tone consistent with your brand and add a personal line, the AI output blends in.

**Q: Is the tool secure for confidential client info?**
A: The service states it does not store your data after generation. I still avoid feeding proprietary details.

## Bottom line
If you spend more than 30 minutes drafting each proposal, an AI generator like ProposalAI can cut that down dramatically. The time saved lets you pitch more, and the modest cost can be recouped after a couple of wins. The tool isn’t a magic win-rate booster, but it does free up brain-space for higher-value work. For freelancers juggling multiple side-hustles, that extra bandwidth is often the real profit.
